blocks.why: Normal night in my own bed before the block starts — bank it while it's free.
Afternoon nap before the JFK redeye; I leave home at 16:55 local and won't be in a bed again until after midnight New York time.
Straight to bed on arrival at the hotel around 00:45 local and sleep through the morning.
Second nap mid-afternoon in New York — the flight home is all night and lands at 11:50 Madrid, so I want to be topped up before report.
Short nap when I get home after the eastbound redeye — kept under three hours so I can still get down early tonight.
Lights out at 20:00 local for the 05:40 report — my body still thinks it's mid-afternoon in New York, so this one needs a dark room and no screens.
Full nine hours after a fourteen-hour four-sector day, and a lie-in before the Singapore report at 11:10.
Landed Singapore at breakfast time after being up all night — six hours in the hotel to clear the debt, then out into the daylight.
Proper local night in Singapore, up at 07:30 with three hours to spare before the 11:10 report.
Home from a thirteen-and-a-half hour westbound — expect to go out cold and wake early, which is normal coming back from the Far East.
Top-up nap on the first day off to cover the early waking, then get outside in the afternoon light to pull the clock back to Madrid.
Days off — hold a fixed 23:30 to 07:30 so the body clock resets to base time.
Same routine again; consistency is what actually moves the clock, not the number of days off.
Third settled night at home, fully back on Madrid time now.
Last full night before the Dubai redeye — sleep in a little later than usual to shorten the day ahead.
Nap in the afternoon dip and be up by 16:00 local, out the door at 16:55 for a 20:20 report.
Into the Dubai hotel around 07:45 local after a full night on the flight deck — six hours with the blackouts shut, no more, or I'll wreck tonight.
Local night in Dubai; two sleeps in the layover is what makes the second night flight survivable.
The big one — a long afternoon nap before a 21:40 report on a duty that lands Madrid at three in the morning.
Home about 05:00 after the clocks went back overnight; sleep straight through the morning and take the free hour as a gift.
Midnight to half eight — deliberately late so I'm rested for a duty that finishes at three in the morning body time.
Short top-up before leaving home at 12:10 UTC; São Paulo doesn't land until 22:25 local and that's 02:25 to me.
In the São Paulo hotel by 23:20 local — go straight down, it's already the small hours on my clock so sleep will come easily.
Late-morning nap in São Paulo before the overnight home; this duty runs straight through my 02:00–06:00 window.
Home at 08:20 local off the redeye — five and a half hours only, so I can still sleep tonight and salvage the two days off.
Back to a normal night at base and start dragging the clock earlier for Sunday's 05:00 standby.
Full night before an afternoon standby that could run to 22:00 local or beyond if I'm called.
Insurance nap before standby starts at 13:00 — if the phone goes late in the window I'll be flying into the night on this.
Standby released at 22:00, home by 23:25 — get down quickly, tomorrow is about winding the clock back for a 05:00 report.
Afternoon nap to bank sleep, because nobody actually gets a full night before an 03:00 alarm.
In bed at 20:30 local for a 03:00 wake-up — I'll only get six and a half at best, hence the nap earlier.
If standby passes uncalled, a short nap after release at 14:00 local to clear the deficit from the 03:00 start.
Straight night before a civilised 11:10 report — no nap needed for this one.
Daytime crossing into Dubai, hotel just before midnight local — a normal eight hours on Dubai time.
Second Dubai night, shifted an hour later on purpose to start leaning toward tomorrow's all-night duty.
Long afternoon nap before the 21:40 report — same pattern that worked on the first Dubai pairing.
Home around 05:00 after the overnight; sleep the morning out, then stay up so tonight goes to plan.
Clean night at home before Boston; the return the next day is a redeye so this is the last unbroken sleep for a while.
Early to bed in Boston at 21:30 local — it's a one-night stop, so I stay on Madrid time rather than trying to flip.
Nap late morning Boston time before a 14:35 report on a redeye landing Madrid at 05:35.
Home by 07:30 local off the last redeye of the block — sleep the morning, then get out in the daylight.
First proper reset night at home base.
Second reset night to finish the period back on Madrid time.

conflicts.statement: 13/10 is printed as LIB, but the JFK-MAD duty that reported on 12/10 doesn't finish until 12:20 local on the 13th, so the day off only really starts once I'm home around 13:45.
options: Treat 13/10 as a recovery day, not a free day, and protect the 20:00 bedtime
Ask crewing whether the day off is meant to be the 13th or the 14th
Accept it and use the short afternoon nap plus an early night as planned

conflicts.statement: Report is 05:40 local, meaning a 04:15 departure from home and a 03:45 alarm, but I land back from New York the previous midday with a body clock six hours west — I'm being asked to fall asleep at what feels like 14:00 and wake at what feels like 21:45.
options: Take the 12:15Z recovery nap on the 13th but cap it at two hours so the early night still works
Blackout, cool room and no caffeine after arrival on the 13th
Raise it with the operator as a low-quality sleep opportunity ahead of a fourteen-hour four-sector day

conflicts.statement: Every other duty in the roster reports 90 minutes before departure; 14/10 prints 05:40 against an 06:40 departure, which is only 60 minutes.
options: Plan on the printed 05:40 as I have done
Confirm with crewing whether short-haul carries a 60-minute offset or the line is a misprint
Build in a 15-minute buffer at home in case the report is actually 05:10

conflicts.statement: Four sectors from an 05:40 report to a 19:59 finish is about 14h20 of duty starting inside the window of circadian low, and the last sector lands at 19:29 after roughly 16 hours awake.
options: Front-load caffeine before the FCO turn rather than late in the day
Use the FRA turnaround for a controlled rest break on the ground
Flag cumulative fatigue to the operator if any sector runs late

conflicts.statement: Spain moves CEST to CET at 03:00 local while I'm airborne on DXB-MAD, so the printed 03:10 arrival is CET; I gain an hour on the clock but the duty is still a full night on the flight deck ending at 02:10Z.
options: Use the extra hour for the recovery sleep, not for a later bedtime
Double-check the crew bus and hotel bookings are quoting post-change local time
Confirm the operator's fatigue calculation is using UTC, not local, for this duty

conflicts.statement: São Paulo is a single overnight — about 15h15 hotel to hotel with a four-hour shift — and the flight home departs 16:05 local and runs straight through 02:00 to 06:00 body time.
options: Take the pre-duty nap at 11:30 local São Paulo as planned
Agree in-flight rest order early and take the first break, which falls nearest the nadir
Ask for the layover to be extended if this pairing repeats next month

conflicts.statement: Standby starts 05:00 local, so I'm awake and potentially reporting at 03:00 body time, and this comes two days after a standby that ran to 22:00 local — the sleep in between has to be moved forward by nearly three hours.
options: Use the 31/10 afternoon nap plus a 20:30 bedtime to build the shift
Ask crewing whether a callout early in this window can be given a later report
If called out for a full duty at 05:00, declare the reduced sleep opportunity before accepting

conflicts.statement: Three duties in six days finish between 02:40 and 05:55 local at MAD (04/11 DXB-MAD, 07/11 BOS-MAD, on top of 27/10 GRU-MAD), each eating the whole of the 02:00-06:00 window.
options: Protect the split sleep pattern on each layover — a post-duty sleep and a pre-duty nap, never one long one
Keep the recovery mornings at home short so the following night stays intact
Raise cumulative night-finish exposure with the operator when bidding next month
